Introduction In 2022, Massachusetts Port Authority (Massport) launched “Net Zero by 2031,” outlining plans to reduce Massport-controlled sources of emissions through operational improvements and efficient infrastructure (Massport 2025b). They plan to achieve these goals through energy conservation and efficiency, enabling renewable energy resources, and alternative ground transportation. Massport established 2019 data as their baseline year, at which time Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) represented roughly 92% of the 877,947 metric tons of carbon dioxide (CO ) equivalent (Massport 2025c). SAF is a commercially available drop-in fuel 2 made from biomass and waste feedstocks and is chemically identical to and meets the same fuel quality specifications as Jet A. Use of SAF at Massport-owned airports is one method to meet their goals. SAF can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by up to 90% dependent upon both the feedstock and technology pathway (Prussi et al. 2021). Massport launched a Massachusetts and New England Regional SAF Hub in June 2025 to unite industries and sectors for the purpose of developing strategies, partnerships, and policy frameworks to accelerate SAF adoption (Massport 2025a). The working group of this effort released a report Recommendations to the Governor on Accelerating the Adoption of Sustainable Aviation Fuels in Massachusetts and New England, which established a plan to incentivize the use of SAF as well as to develop a regional SAF industry (Massport 2025a). As a part of this effort, Massport funded the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) to prepare a SAF study. This study evaluated the potential SAF production in New England and a logistics assessment for using SAF in the region regardless of where it is produced. The study includes background information on national and regional jet fuel use, SAF production technologies and plants, a biomass resource assessment for 10 selected airports (Table 1), a techno-economic analysis (TEA) of a New England-based SAF biorefinery, and a review of regional jet fuel and SAF logistics. These airports were selected to represent diverse geographies, fuel volumes, and facility types. This report refers to both jet fuel and Jet A.
